q-49524.prompt: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{@@D1@@}+\frac{1}{@@D2@@})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
q-49524.solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{@@D1@@}+\frac{1}{@@D2@@})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{@@D1@@}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{@@D2@@}\,\text{d}x \\  & =@@INV@@\operatorname{ln}⁡|@@D1@@|-@@INV@@\operatorname{ln}⁡|@@D2@@|+C \\  & =@@INV@@\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{@@D1@@}{@@D2@@}|+@@INV@@\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =@@INV@@\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{@@D1@@}{@@D2@@}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.
